name: fabflows
description: Routes work from an expensive lead model to tool-scoped worker agents -- explorer and researcher on Haiku, editor and test-runner on Sonnet, refuter and investigator on Opus -- and makes the lead re-verify what they report instead of trusting it. Adds fabflows:build, a deterministic loop in which an Opus builder implements a spec and a fresh reviewer returns ACCEPT or REWORK. Ships an ACTIVE guard hook that asks the user before package installs and package runners such as npx, and denies them in workers (one exception: pypdf into a literal scratchpad --target with --isolated), and blocks commits and pushes to a default branch, destructive shell commands, and reads or writes of credential files, and destructive commands written into a Makefile, npm script or shell script; the guard fails open, so a bug degrades to no guard rather than a blocked session. The using-fabflows skill is the session entrypoint and standing opt-in to the build loop. The brainstorming skill turns a rough idea into a spec the build loop can take: the lead asks bounded rounds of questions with recommended answers, workers read the codebase and the web, and the refuter attacks the draft lens by lens before the spec is written. The fabflows-setup skill points the repository at a tracker (GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear) in a committed .claude/fabflows.json; the spec then lives in the linked ticket instead of docs/specs/, the ticket skill keeps that ticket current through its MCP tools and, at each session start, closes or cancels tickets whose PR merged or closed outside the session, and the ticket.js hook requires Refs and Spec trailers on commits and the key in the PR title. The trace skill writes an audit trace report outside the repo: every merged change with its PR approvers, ticket, approved spec hash, Compliance section and flags such as no-ticket or self-approved.
